phpwcms before 1.9.53, 1.12.7 and 2.0.0-beta.4 contains a host header poisoning vulnerability that allows unauthenticated attackers to control password reminder links by sending a forged X-Forwarded-Host header. Attackers can submit the public password reminder form for a victim so the emailed {LOGIN_URL} points to an attacker host, capturing the new password when the victim logs in there.

AIOStreams 2.9.0 through 2.38.1 contains an information disclosure vulnerability in makeRequest() that leaks the internal secret header by matching URLs against INTERNAL_URL using a string-prefix check. Attackers can supply a custom addon manifest URL or redirect to a prefix-matching host or port to capture the secret and directly call internal addon routes.

Contiki-NG through 5.2 contains an out-of-bounds write vulnerability in the MPL multicast engine that allows remote unauthenticated attackers to corrupt memory via unchecked seed ID lengths. Attackers can send near-maximum-size MPL messages with an S=3 option in a short hop-by-hop header, causing data_message_expiration() to write 16 bytes past uip_buf and crash the node.

FontForge through 20251009 contains a heap out-of-bounds write vulnerability in PcfReadEncodingsNames() that allows attackers to corrupt memory via negative glyph indices from truncated PCF encodings tables. Attackers can supply a crafted .pcf file imported through the GUI or scripting Import() command to write before the encs array, causing crashes or potential code execution.

Convoy before 26.6.0 contains an information disclosure vulnerability that allows authenticated dashboard users to read other organisations' data due to missing membership checks on /ui/organisations/{orgID}/ read routes. Attackers who know another organisation's ID can request members, invites/pending, and projects endpoints to obtain member emails, roles, pending invitee emails, and project lists.

The AIL Framework web application contains a stored cross-site scripting (XSS) vulnerability in its dashboard templates. In the home dashboard (dashboard.html), the hunter trackers dashboard (trackers_dashboard.html), and the objects dashboard (objs_dashboard.html), object global identifiers (GIDs) derived from filenames or message IDs were interpolated directly into inline JavaScript event handler attributes (onmouseenter/onmouseleave) within HTML anchor tags. Because the GID value was placed inside a single-quoted JavaScript string literal within an HTML attribute, an attacker who could control the GID value (for example, by crafting a filename or message ID containing a single quote) could break out of the string context and inject arbitrary JavaScript code that would execute in the context of any user viewing the dashboard.

Additionally, in dynamically generated JavaScript code within the same templates, object identifiers were concatenated into HTML strings and inline event handler registrations without sufficient encoding, presenting a similar injection surface. The AJAX tooltip lookup also concatenated the raw GID into a URL without encoding, which could be leveraged for further manipulation.

The vulnerability requires that an attacker be able to influence the GID value stored in the application (e.g., through a file upload or message creation with a crafted name) and that a victim subsequently visits one of the affected dashboard pages and hovers over the affected object link. Successful exploitation allows execution of arbitrary JavaScript in the victim's browser session, potentially leading to session hijacking, data exfiltration, or unauthorized actions performed on behalf of the victim.

GFI HelpDesk before 4.99.13 contains an SQL injection vulnerability in the staff group management feature that allows authenticated attackers with administrator privileges to execute arbitrary SQL queries by supplying a crafted title parameter to /admin/index.php?/Base/StaffGroup/InsertSubmit. The Controller_StaffGroup.RunChecks() method concatenates the unsanitized title value directly into a duplicate name lookup query against the staffgroup table, allowing attackers to read or modify database contents.

odf-kit is a TypeScript and JavaScript library for working with OpenDocument Format files. In versions 0.9.8 through 0.14.1, the odsToHtml() renderer inserts document-controlled cell formatting and row height values into HTML style attributes without escaping them. An attacker can craft an ODS file that injects arbitrary HTML attributes or elements, allowing JavaScript execution in the host page's origin when an application inserts the converted output as HTML. This issue is fixed in version 0.14.2.

A vulnerability was found in vijaythapa333 django-student-management-system up to 0d96e62cc4e996e3e77bec1b8e3da3980edf8889. Affected by this issue is the function student_profile_update of the file StudentViews.py of the component Student Profile Update. The manipulation of the argument first_name results in cross site scripting. The attack may be performed from remote. The exploit has been made public and could be used. This product utilizes a rolling release system for continuous delivery, and as such, version information for affected or updated releases is not disclosed. The project was informed of the problem early through an issue report but has not responded yet.

Tabbycat 2.9.0 through 2.12.1 contains an incorrect authorization vulnerability in TournamentViewSet that allows unauthenticated attackers to gain write access because PerTournamentPermissionRequired returns True for views lacking a tournament attribute. Attackers can send POST, PUT, PATCH or DELETE requests to /api/v1/tournaments to create, modify or delete tournaments, cascading deletion to teams and speakers.

MyBibliotheca 3.0.0 before 3.0.4 contains an insecure direct object reference vulnerability that allows authenticated users to modify or delete other users' books via /api/v1/books/<book_id>. Attackers can obtain book UUIDs from recently added books across all owners, then send PUT or DELETE requests to rename, alter, or permanently delete them.

Daptin before 0.13.61 contains an incorrect authorization vulnerability that allows authenticated users to overwrite restricted contacts by sending CardDAV PUT requests to existing contacts. Attackers holding address book Update permission can bypass per-contact row permissions in PutAddressObject to modify protected contacts and confirm their existence.

Anchr before 3.7.2 contains a stored cross-site scripting vulnerability that allows authenticated users to host HTML files by uploading them through the image upload feature with a spoofed image content type. Attackers can upload an .html file served via GET /api/image/:id from the Anchr origin, running script that steals the victim's localStorage session token for account takeover.

MediaInfoLib before 26.10 contains a heap use-after-free vulnerability in the Vorbis setup header parser that allows attackers to trigger reads of freed memory via crafted files. Attackers can supply a crafted Ogg/Vorbis file that makes File_Vorbis::Setup() return early without BS_End_LE(), leaving a stale bitstream pointer that causes crashes or heap disclosure.

MediaInfoLib before 26.10 contains an out-of-bounds read vulnerability in File_Mpegv::Streams_Fill() that allows attackers to read adjacent memory via an uninitialized chroma_format index. Attackers can craft media files that reach Streams_Fill() before Synched_Init(), crashing MediaInfo or embedding applications and possibly exposing static memory in parser output.

The system call verification handlers for smbus_block_read() and smbus_block_pcall() in drivers/smbus/smbus_handlers.c (z_vrfy_smbus_block_read() and z_vrfy_smbus_block_pcall()) validated the device object, the count pointers and (for process call) the send buffer, but never validated the receive buffer (buf / rcv_buf). The call then proceeds into the driver implementation, which runs in supervisor mode and writes the bytes received from the SMBus peripheral through that pointer.

A user-mode thread on a system built with CONFIG_USERSPACE that has been granted access to an SMBus device object can pass an arbitrary address, including kernel data or another thread's memory, as the receive buffer. The driver then writes up to SMBUS_BLOCK_BYTES_MAX (32) bytes of peripheral-supplied data there (the STM32 driver writes as many bytes as the peripheral's length byte announces, up to 255). The address is fully attacker-chosen; the written content comes from the bus and is typically influenceable by the caller through the choice of peripheral and command, or by first writing data to a device that echoes it back.

This breaks the user/kernel isolation boundary: it gives an unprivileged thread a kernel-memory write primitive usable for privilege escalation, or at minimum to corrupt kernel state or crash the system. The fix adds K_SYSCALL_MEMORY_WRITE() checks of the receive buffer for the documented worst case, SMBUS_BLOCK_BYTES_MAX. Systems without CONFIG_USERSPACE are not affected.

The STM32 SMBus driver (drivers/smbus/smbus_stm32.c) implements smbus_block_read() and smbus_block_pcall() by issuing a single i2c_transfer() in which the byte-count byte returned by the peripheral is read directly into the len field of the following i2c_msg. That message then receives data straight into the caller-supplied buffer. Nothing bounds the count, so smbus_stm32_block_read() and smbus_stm32_block_pcall() read up to 255 bytes into a buffer that the SMBus API documents (and the syscall verifiers validate) as holding at most SMBUS_BLOCK_BYTES_MAX (32) bytes.

The count is chosen by the addressed SMBus peripheral. A malicious, counterfeit or faulty device on the bus (for example a removable smart battery, PMBus supply or plug-in module), or anyone able to drive the bus lines, can report a block count above 32 and cause the driver to write up to 223 bytes past the end of the caller's buffer. Callers typically pass a 32-byte stack buffer, as the in-tree smbus block_read shell command does, so the overflow lands on the caller's stack before any caller-side count check can run.

The result is attacker-controlled stack or memory corruption in the context of the calling thread, which can crash the system or potentially be leveraged for code execution. When the call arrives through the smbus_block_read/smbus_block_pcall system calls, the out-of-bounds write happens in supervisor mode beyond the 32-byte region validated for the user thread. The fix receives the block into a driver-local 255-byte buffer and copies it out only when the count is at most SMBUS_BLOCK_BYTES_MAX, returning -ENODATA otherwise.

The OpenThread PSA crypto platform backend in modules/openthread/platform/crypto_psa.c only supported PSA key references. otPlatCryptoAesSetKey() copied aKey->mKeyRef into the AES context unconditionally. On an OpenThread Radio Co-Processor (RCP) build, CONFIG_OPENTHREAD_CRYPTO_PSA does not select CONFIG_OPENTHREAD_PLATFORM_KEY_REF, so OpenThread passes the MAC key as literal bytes and mKeyRef is uninitialized. psa_cipher_encrypt() in otPlatCryptoAesEncrypt() then fails without writing its output, and the error is only caught by an OpenThread assertion that is compiled to a no-op when CONFIG_ASSERT is disabled.

When the RCP handles transmit security in software, AES-CCM* is never keyed. That is the case with Thread 1.2 or later, where CONFIG_OPENTHREAD_MAC_SOFTWARE_TX_SECURITY_ENABLE defaults to y, on a radio driver without IEEE802154_HW_TX_SEC. Every MAC key-id-mode-1 frame goes out with its payload XORed against a single 16-byte pad of stale stack data, reused for every block, and with an unkeyed MIC. CONFIG_OPENTHREAD_CRYPTO_PSA is enabled by default since v4.4.0.

A passive attacker within 802.15.4 radio range can recover the pad from predictable plaintext (for example 6LoWPAN headers) and read the payload of the frames the device transmits. The practical impact is limited. The configuration is not the default (the default Thread version is 1.1), and the same defect makes peers reject every secured data frame, so an affected device cannot exchange data on the network. Received traffic and key distribution are not affected. With CONFIG_ASSERT enabled, the RCP halts on the first secured transmission instead.

A vulnerability has been found in ONLYOFFICE onlyoffice-humhub up to 4.0.0. This impacts the function html of the file notifications/Mention.php of the component Mention Notification Handler. Such manipulation of the argument Comment leads to cross site scripting. The attack can be executed remotely. The exploit has been disclosed to the public and may be used. The vendor was contacted early about this disclosure but did not respond in any way.

A vulnerability was determined in humhub lets-meet up to 1.2.1. Affected by this vulnerability is the function NewInviteNotification::html of the file notifications/NewInviteNotification.php of the component Notification Rendering. Executing a manipulation can lead to cross site scripting. The attack may be performed from remote. The exploit has been publicly disclosed and may be utilized. Upgrading to version 1.2.2 addresses this issue. This patch is called 6c82534ffcb90e74229671a76caef1a8285c5190. Upgrading the affected component is advised.

A potential security vulnerability has been identified in the HP Hotkey UWP Service, which might allow escalation of privilege. HP is releasing mitigation for the potential vulnerability. Customers using HP Programmable Key are recommended to update HP Hotkey Support.

DreameHome cloud API before 2026-10-14 contained an insecure direct object reference vulnerability in the POST /smart-app/meari-cloud/redirectAndLogin endpoint that allows authenticated attackers to obtain another user's Meari camera-platform identity and session credentials by supplying that user's uid. The endpoint used the caller-supplied uid to select the Meari account without verifying that it belonged to the account authenticated by the Dreame-Auth token. Attackers can obtain target uids through public forum profiles and an email-to-uid lookup, and use the leaked credentials to access live video, microphone audio, the camera speaker, and stored recordings of Meari-backed cameras.

DreameHome device sharing and MQTT broker before 2026-10-26 contained an incorrect authorization vulnerability that allows former share recipients to keep receiving a device's MQTT status messages after the owner revokes sharing. Revocation removed application access and the device-command API rejected the former recipient, but the broker still accepted subscriptions to the device's status topic using the DID, owner UID, and model exposed during sharing, allowing continued monitoring of the home's map data and device status.

DreameHome cloud API before 2026-10-14 contained an insecure direct object reference vulnerability in the POST /dreame-user-iot/token/rtc2 endpoint that allows authenticated attackers to obtain an Agora RTC token for another user's device by supplying its device DID and owner UID. The endpoint issued the token without verifying device ownership, allowing attackers to join the device's live-video channel and publish video under the targeted device's identity.
Rejected reason: This issue was not considered a security vulnerability.

An out-of-bounds write issue exists in padded block cipher decryption in AWS-LC. It affects applications that decrypt CBC or ECB ciphertext with PKCS7 padding over multiple calls into the minimum documented output buffer. A remote user who supplies crafted ciphertext might crash the application or corrupt adjacent memory. Affected are all versions of AWS-LC before 5.7.0, AWS-LC-FIPS 4.x before 4.2.0, AWS-LC-FIPS 3.x before 3.6.0, and AWS-LC-FIPS 2.x before 2.0.18.



To remediate this issue, users should upgrade to AWS-LC 5.7.0, AWS-LC-FIPS 4.2.0, or AWS-LC-FIPS 3.6.0.



AWS-LC-FIPS 2.0.18 is also fixed; AWS-LC-FIPS 2.x reaches end of support in April 2027.

A security flaw has been discovered in RainyGao DocSys up to 2.02.91. Affected by this vulnerability is the function downloadDocRS of the file src/com/DocSystem/controller/DocController.java. Performing a manipulation of the argument path results in path traversal. It is possible to initiate the attack remotely. The exploit has been released to the public and may be used for attacks. The project was informed of the problem early through an issue report but has not responded yet.

A weakness has been identified in FredrikNoren ungit 1.5.30. Affected by this issue is the function credentialsOption of the file source/git-api.js of the component Remote Git API. Executing a manipulation of the argument Remote can lead to os command injection. It is possible to launch the attack remotely. The exploit has been made available to the public and could be used for attacks. The project was informed of the problem early through an issue report but has not responded yet.

A security vulnerability has been detected in FredrikNoren ungit 1.5.30. This affects the function writeUserConfig of the file source/server.js of the component API Server. The manipulation of the argument launchCommand leads to missing authentication. The attack can be initiated remotely. The exploit has been disclosed publicly and may be used. The project was informed of the problem early through an issue report but has not responded yet.

WPC Product Options for WooCommerce before 4.0.9 contains a price manipulation vulnerability that allows unauthenticated attackers to purchase products at an arbitrary price by submitting crafted wpcpo-* option data with a negative price in an add-to-cart request. Attackers can exploit the add_cart_item_data() function in includes/class-cart.php, which stores client-supplied price values without validation and carries them into the order total via before_calculate_totals(), to checkout products at zero or arbitrary cost.

Dynamic Product Gallery for WooCommerce before 3.6.2 contains a stored cross-site scripting vulnerability that allows authenticated attackers with Contributor-level access or above to inject arbitrary JavaScript via the product_id attribute of the [wc_product_dgallery] and [wc_product_dynamic_gallery] shortcodes. The parse_shortcode_product_dynamic_gallery() function passes product_id only through esc_attr(), and get_gallery_main() prints it unescaped into the a3-wc-dynamic-gallery-init-inline-script inline script as part of a JavaScript variable name, so a value such as 342;alert(document.domain)// breaks out of the declaration. The injected script executes in the browser of any user who views the post, including editors or administrators who preview or approve it.
An arbitrary remote code execution vulnerability exists in HPE Morpheus Manager.

Missing authorization in Kibana Security AI Assistant conversation deletion can allow an authenticated user with access to the assistant to delete other users' conversations in the same space. The delete-all operation can issue a query without an ownership filter using the assistant's internal Elasticsearch client. A user can consequently delete conversation history that they do not own or have permission to modify.

Memory Allocation with Excessive Size Value (CWE-789) in Packetbeat can lead to denial of service via a specially crafted, malformed Cassandra protocol message. An unauthenticated attacker who can send traffic on a network segment that Packetbeat monitors can cause Packetbeat to allocate excessive memory and terminate. Elastic Agent is also affected when the Network Packet Capture integration monitors Cassandra traffic, because it uses the same protocol decoder.

Hermes Agent is an open-source autonomous AI agent built by Nous Research for running tool-using workflows across CLI, desktop, and messaging interfaces. From 0.21.6 to 0.23.1, when Bot Desktop is hosted inside a non-local terminal backend, the agent process reads a backend-writable screen environment file without validating keys or values and merges its entries into the environment of processes started on the agent machine. Specifically, when terminal.backend is set to docker or ssh (or a plugin backend declaring supports_streams) with placement auto or terminal, _published() in tools/bot_desktop/sandbox_host.py accepts arbitrary KEY=VALUE lines from the hermes-bot-desktop env file and propagates them via tools/bot_desktop/runtime.py into the browser harness, computer-use helpers, and local terminal children. Code running inside the terminal backend can therefore set variables such as LD_PRELOAD, DYLD_INSERT_LIBRARIES, or PATH and gain code execution on the agent machine as the gateway user upon a subsequent browser or computer-use spawn, exposing credentials, tokens, and session history under the Hermes home directory. The default local backend, backends that cannot host a screen (Modal, Daytona, and Vercel), and Hermes Cloud in its default configuration are not affected. This issue is fixed in version 0.23.2.

Uncontrolled resource allocation in Kibana exception-list filter creation can lead to denial of service. An authenticated user with access to the Security solution can submit a specially crafted request containing a large number of exception-list identifiers. Kibana can create an unbounded number of concurrent operations while resolving those identifiers, exhausting memory and crashing the Kibana process.

Certain Fleet APIs in Kibana expose stored credentials to authenticated users who do not have the Fleet Settings: Read privilege. For example, a user with the Fleet Agent policies: Read privilege can retrieve credentials through Fleet output and agent binary download source APIs. The disclosed credentials could allow the attacker to authenticate to connected backend systems.

An issue in Kibana allows Elasticsearch transforms in directly uploaded integration packages to run with Kibana's internal system identity instead of the installing user's privileges. A user with Integrations: All and Agent policies: All privileges in a single Kibana space could access or modify data they are not authorized to access, including agent policies from other spaces. This could disclose sensitive information or lead to command execution on managed Elastic Agent hosts.

Incorrect authorization in Elasticsearch columnar indices can bypass field-level security for geo_shape values. An authenticated user with access to an affected index can obtain denied geometry values through the internal source-geometry representation even when field-level security excludes the corresponding field. This discloses field data that the user is not authorized to read.

Elasticsearch ES|QL query responses can disclose dataset storage locations and provider identity details to users who are allowed to query a dataset but cannot read its definition. Storage paths and storage-client error text can appear in read-failure messages or query-profile plan strings. An authenticated dataset reader can obtain this information without permission to view the dataset configuration. This issue does not disclose stored credentials or the dataset contents beyond the caller's query access.

Elasticsearch ES|QL data-source and dataset registration can write storage credentials or pre-signed URL signatures to the audit log in plaintext. In affected versions, request definitions are not appropriately filtered before request-body or URL-query auditing. An attacker with access to these logs can obtain credentials for the customer's external storage. The issue affects deployments with ES|QL federation enabled and audit logging configured to record the affected request information.

Uncontrolled resource allocation in Elasticsearch mapping updates can lead to denial of service. An authenticated user with index-management privileges can submit specially crafted mapping updates that are expanded into multiple large in-memory representations. The amplification during request parsing and mapping updates can exhaust heap memory and crash an Elasticsearch node.

Uncontrolled resource consumption in Elasticsearch query parsing can lead to denial of service. An authenticated user with search permissions can submit a specially crafted query containing an excessive number of clauses. Expanding those clauses in memory before enforcing query complexity limits can exhaust heap memory and crash an Elasticsearch node.

An issue was discovered in Kibana where a user with the Synthetics All privilege in one space can access Fleet agent policy metadata from other spaces through a product API endpoint. This could lead to the unauthorized disclosure of operational metadata across spaces the user is not authorized to view.

Unconstrained S3 endpoint settings in Elasticsearch ES|QL data sources can cause requests containing storage credentials to be sent to an attacker-controlled host. A user with data-source management privileges can configure a custom endpoint without the intended host restriction. On opted-in commercial Elastic Cloud Hosted deployments, the issue can also disclose workload-identity tokens and expose customer cloud resources outside Elasticsearch. Self-managed deployments are affected by the storage-endpoint path only.

Missing authorization in Kibana Cases alert attachments can allow an authenticated user with permission to add case comments or attachments to modify case-link metadata in documents they are not authorized to access. An attacker can add false case links and prevent legitimate case linkage by exhausting the alert's case-link limit. Writes are limited to the kibana.alert.case_ids field in indices that Kibana's internal account can read and update and whose mappings accept that field. One of the two authorization defects was fixed earlier in 8.19.22, 9.4.8 and 9.5.5; the fixed versions listed in this advisory address both defects.

A relative path traversal vulnerability in Kibana Fleet and Elastic Agent allows an authenticated user with both Fleet Integrations: All and Agent policies: All privileges to distribute a malicious integration policy to managed Elastic Agents. A vulnerable Elastic Agent processing that policy for a component that runs in an isolated unit can modify or delete files outside the component's intended runtime directory with the privileges of the Elastic Agent process. This can cause loss of files or persistent denial of service on affected hosts.

A vulnerability was detected in FredrikNoren ungit 1.5.30. This vulnerability affects unknown code of the file source/git-api.js of the component /api/clone. The manipulation of the argument url results in argument injection. The attack can be launched remotely. The exploit is now public and may be used. The project was informed of the problem early through an issue report but has not responded yet.

open62541 1.5.0 through 1.5.10 contains a use-after-free and double free vulnerability in the lookupRefType() function in src/util/ua_util.c that allows attackers to corrupt the heap of the server process by supplying a RelativePath string resolved through UA_RelativePath_parseWithServer(). When the path names a ReferenceType with a string or GUID NodeId, the function returns a shallow copy of the browse result's NodeId and frees its identifier, causing the identifier to be freed a second time when the parsed path is cleared, which attackers can exploit to crash the server process.

Lookyloo is a web-based URL capture and analysis platform. Prior to the fix, the authorization mechanism for private captures (seed-based access control) was not consistently enforced at the data access layer. The capture_cache method and numerous internal methods (get_info, get_meta, get_statistics, get_modules_responses, get_data, get_video, get_screenshot, get_har, get_cookies, get_storage_state, get_frames, get_console_messages, get_capture, get_ressource, misp_export, lacus_export, ai_export, comparator functions, and others) could be invoked with only a capture UUID without validating the required seed token. This meant that API endpoints and internal code paths that called these methods directly could return private capture data to unauthenticated users or users lacking the correct seed. The before_request hook in the web interface provided a partial check, but the underlying data layer did not enforce it, creating an inconsistent authorization boundary. An attacker who knew or guessed a private capture UUID could potentially access sensitive data including rendered screenshots, HAR files, downloaded files, cookies, storage state, console messages, and MISP exports through various REST API endpoints and web routes. The fix introduces a LookylooPrivateCapture exception raised at the cache layer when a private capture is accessed without a valid seed, refactors the API to pass CaptureCache objects (already validated) rather than raw UUIDs, and ensures all web and API endpoints propagate the session-known seed or admin status to the data access layer. Background processes use an explicit unsafe=True flag to bypass the check, as they operate server-side with full trust.

A buffer over-read vulnerability in Elasticsearch transport decompression can expose data from other requests. The LZ4 decoder can read beyond the declared compressed block into a shared network buffer. A remote attacker who can reach an affected transport interface can send a specially crafted compressed request and obtain data from outside their own request. Exploitation of the exposed remote-cluster transport interface does not require authentication.
Server-side request forgery in Profile Data Roaming Service (PDRS) allows an authorized attacker to elevate privileges over a network.
Improper neutralization of input during web page generation ('cross-site scripting') in Authentication Methods Portal Extension allows an unauthorized attacker to elevate privileges over a network.
Authorization bypass through user-controlled key in Microsoft Clarity allows an unauthorized attacker to elevate privileges over a network.

Missing authorization in Kibana Security AI Assistant conversation deletion can allow an authenticated assistant user to permanently delete a shared or global conversation owned by another user in the same space. The individual-delete path can treat read access to a shared conversation as permission to delete it without checking ownership. The deleted conversation history is lost to its legitimate owner.
Server-side request forgery in Azure Machine Learning allows an authorized attacker to elevate privileges over a network.
Improper access control in Azure Site Recovery allows an unauthorized attacker to elevate privileges over a network.
Incorrect authorization in Azure Managed Service Identity allows an authorized attacker to elevate privileges over a network.
Improper certificate validation in Microsoft Office PowerPoint allows an unauthorized attacker to execute code over a network.

A flaw was found in rsyslog. A remote, unauthenticated attacker can cause a Denial of Service (DoS) by sending a specially crafted log message with an unusual timestamp. When the service processes this message using weekday formatting templates, an out-of-bounds memory read occurs, causing the application to crash.

React is a JavaScript library for building user interfaces. In versions prior to 19.0.9, 19.1.10, 19.2.9 and 19.3.1, react-server-dom-webpack, react-server-dom-parcel, and react-server-dom-turbopack are vulnerable to denial of service. Specially crafted HTTP requests sent to server function endpoints can cause out-of-memory exceptions or excessive CPU usage. This issue is fixed in versions 19.0.9, 19.1.10, 19.2.9 and 19.3.1.

The ggml-rpc server suffers from an uninitialized heap memory disclosure vulnerability where the alloc_buffer function provides new clients with buffers containing stale data from previously freed allocations. This allows an unauthenticated remote attacker to perform an in-bounds read via get_tensor to recover sensitive information, such as model weights or KV-cache data, belonging to other clients sharing the same server.

An issue was discovered in Elasticsearch where specially crafted compressed payloads can cause an infinite loop. A low-privileged authenticated user can submit a malformed payload to a product API endpoint that causes the node to enter a permanent CPU loop, occupying a request-processing thread indefinitely. This can progressively exhaust the node's processing capacity, degrading or denying access to product features, and requiring a restart of the affected node to recover.

Use of a default cryptographic key in the instance registration component in Amazon SSM Agent before 3.3.5226.0 on AWS-provided Windows Server AMIs released before 2026-09-09 might allow local users without administrative privileges to obtain the instance's Default Host Management Configuration role credentials via the registration key shared by all instances launched from the same AMI.



To remediate this issue, users should replace affected instances with instances launched from AWS Windows Server AMIs released on or after 2026-09-09, which include SSM Agent 3.3.5226.0 or later. Upgrading the agent in place does not replace the shared key, and deleting the agent's Vault breaks instances managed through Default Host Management Configuration.
Improper authorization in M365 Copilot allows an authorized attacker to elevate privileges over a network.
Improper authentication in Azure Event Grid allows an unauthorized attacker to elevate privileges over a network.

Improper neutralization of special elements used in an os command ('os command injection') in Azure Managed Instance for Apache Cassandra allows an unauthorized attacker to execute code over an adjacent network.
Missing authorization in Azure AI Foundry allows an unauthorized attacker to disclose information over a network.
Authentication bypass by spoofing in Azure DevTest Labs allows an unauthorized attacker to perform spoofing over a network.
Improper limitation of a pathname to a restricted directory ('path traversal') in Microsoft Office SharePoint allows an authorized attacker to execute code over a network.
Improper neutralization of input during web page generation ('cross-site scripting') in Azure Portal allows an unauthorized attacker to perform spoofing over a network.
Incorrect authorization in Azure Machine Learning allows an unauthorized attacker to disclose information over a network.

SQL injection in WHMCS could allow an authenticated client with View & Manage Contacts permission to retrieve other clients' personal, billing, and support information, as well as administrator account records and password hashes.
SQL injection in WHMCS could allow an unauthenticated user to retrieve clients' personal and support information, as well as administrator account records and password hashes.
An authenticated WHMCS client could potentially leverage this flaw to read sensitive configuration files on the WHMCS host, including database credentials, and to execute code on the server.

EUSurvey through 1.6, prior to commit 0669a36, contains a path traversal vulnerability in the survey import function that allows authenticated attackers with the Form Manager role to execute arbitrary code on the server. The POST /noform/management/importSurvey endpoint trusts archive entry names when SurveyExportHelper writes imported files through FileService, so a crafted survey archive can write a JSP file outside the survey storage directory into the application directory, where Tomcat executes it with the privileges of the EUSurvey process

EUSurvey 1.5.5 through 1.6, prior to commit d5295d5, contains a missing authorization vulnerability in the POST /forms/bulkchange endpoint that allows any authenticated user to take over or delete other users' surveys. SurveyController accepts arbitrary survey IDs and privilege values, and BulkExecutor applies the requested access-right changes or deletion without checking whether the requester can manage those surveys, allowing an ordinary ROLE_USER account to grant itself full control of another user's survey, read its draft and results, edit the form, manage its invitations, or delete it.

EUSurvey through 1.6, prior to commit a4161a9, contains a weak password recovery mechanism that allows attackers who obtain a still-valid password-reset link to take over accounts that use a local EUSurvey password. The /auth/reset/ flow checks only the age of a reset code and does not invalidate it after the password is changed, and issuing a newer link leaves earlier links active, so a used or superseded link remains valid for up to 24 hours from issuance and can be reused to set a new password, sign in as the affected user, and lock that user out.

EUSurvey through 1.6, prior to commit 118facd, contains an authorization bypass vulnerability in the public POST /runner/draft/runner endpoint that allows unauthenticated attackers to overwrite another participant's saved draft and obtain its private invitation token. The draft save handler in RunnerController and AnswerService loads an existing draft by invitation alone without checking that the submitted survey, participation group and invitation belong together, then replaces the draft's answers, reassigns it to the submitted survey, and returns a resume link containing the private invitation token.

EUSurvey through 1.6, prior to commit edb5021, contains an incorrect authorization vulnerability in the GET /settings/shareEdit/{shareId} and POST /settings/shares handlers that allows any authenticated user to read or modify another user's contact share. The ownership check in SettingsController denies access only when a condition is both true and false, so it never denies access, allowing an ordinary account without Contact Management privileges to read the names and email addresses in a share and to rename it, change its recipient or access mode, or replace its contacts.

EUSurvey through 1.6, prior to commit 4bf95a3, contains an authorization bypass vulnerability in the GET /preparepublishedcontribution/{id} endpoint that allows unauthenticated attackers to read private responses submitted to published surveys. The contribution PDF handler in ContributionController looks up a response by its sequential database ID and skips the normal response access checks, so attackers can enumerate IDs to retrieve other respondents' answers, including free-text answers that may contain personal data, across surveys.

EUSurvey 1.4.4.6738 through 1.6, prior to commit de1145c, contains an SQL injection vulnerability in the public results page GET /publication/{shortname} that allows unauthenticated attackers to infer non-public response data. ReportingService builds a SQL column expression from part of a user-supplied filter parameter name and inserts it directly into the query, so a visitor to any survey that publishes its results can inject boolean conditions and use the presence or absence of public result rows to infer private reporting data, including response data and respondent metadata from other surveys.

EUSurvey through 1.6, prior to commit de1145c, contains an authorization bypass vulnerability in the public POST /editcontribution/{code} endpoint that allows unauthenticated attackers to overwrite another respondent's submitted answers. The handler in ContributionController selects the survey and answer set from body parameters by numeric contribution ID and never checks that the private edit code in the URL matches that contribution, so an attacker who knows a contribution ID can replace its saved answers without the respondent's edit link.

EUSurvey 1.5.2 through 1.6, prior to commit ffd5da7, contains a missing authorization vulnerability in the public POST /runner/delphiUpdate endpoint that allows unauthenticated attackers to submit responses to Delphi surveys after the owner has closed them. DelphiController checks only that the survey exists and is a Delphi survey and skips the closure check enforced by the normal survey page, so an attacker who knows the survey and question IDs can create new responses that remain in the survey's results.

EUSurvey through 1.6, prior to commit 4bf95a3, contains a blind SQL injection vulnerability in the GET /dashboard/surveys endpoint that allows authenticated attackers with the Form Manager role to infer data from the main application database. SurveyService inserts unrecognized sort values directly into the ORDER BY clause of a native query, so attackers can supply SQL expressions and use response timing to infer any data readable by the application's database account, including data outside the surveys listed on their dashboard.

EUSurvey 1.5.2 through 1.6, prior to commit bb7432c, contains a stored cross-site scripting vulnerability in Delphi survey explanations that allows survey participants to execute arbitrary JavaScript in other users' browsers. Explanations submitted to POST /runner/delphiUpdate are stored by AnswerExplanationService without sanitization and rendered as HTML in delphiAnswersTable.jsp, so an injected event handler runs in the EUSurvey origin with the session of any participant or survey manager who views the answers table.

EUSurvey through 1.6, prior to commit 6db6147, contains an insecure direct object reference vulnerability in the GET /exports/checkNew endpoint that allows authenticated attackers to read the names of other users' finished exports and suppress their notifications. ExportsController trusts a user ID supplied by the browser without checking it against the authenticated session, and ExportService marks every export it returns as notified, so the owner never receives the notice that their export is ready.

EUSurvey through 1.6, prior to commit 03cc974, contains a blind server-side request forgery vulnerability in PDF export that allows authenticated attackers with the Form Manager role to make the server send HTTP or HTTPS requests to internal services. Question titles saved through POST /{shortname}/management/edit are rendered as raw markup in runnercontentinnerpdf.jsp, and the PDFRenderer resource loader fetches referenced images without checking whether the destination is on an internal network when a response is exported as a PDF.

EUSurvey through 1.6, prior to commit 4ff1ba0, contains a missing authorization vulnerability in the GET /pdf/survey/{surveyId} endpoint that allows attackers holding a valid invitation for one survey to download a different survey's restricted questionnaire PDF without signing in. PDFController checks that the supplied invitation and participation group are active but not that they belong to the requested survey, exposing questions intended only for invited respondents of any published survey that allows PDF access.

Pelican 4.12.0 contains an OS command injection vulnerability in pelican-import. An attacker-controlled wp:post_name from a WordPress XML export is used in an output filename that is interpolated into a Pandoc command passed to subprocess.call with shell=True. On POSIX systems, command substitution in the slug is evaluated when a user imports the crafted export.

n8n is an open source workflow automation platform. Prior to 1.123.90 and 2.14.0, the invitation acceptance endpoint accepts inviter and invitee user IDs without a signed invitation token, allowing any preexisting member to take over a pending new user account. A member with permission to list users can read the ID of a pending account and set its password without authentication, then log in as that user, including as an admin when the invitation has the admin role. Exploitation requires an invitation that has not been accepted yet. This issue is fixed in versions 1.123.90 and 2.14.0.

n8n is an open source workflow automation platform. Prior to 2.47.6, 2.48.3, and 3.2.2, the password reset link and role change operations do not protect the instance owner account from users with a custom instance role. A user whose custom instance role includes user management permissions can obtain a password reset link for the owner and take over the owner account, or change the owner's role, gaining full control of the instance. Exploitation requires the custom roles feature and a custom instance role with user management permissions. This issue is fixed in versions 2.47.6, 2.48.3, and 3.2.2.

AutoGPT is a workflow automation platform for creating, deploying, and managing continuous artificial intelligence agents. In versions 0.6.26 through 0.7.4, AutoGPT Platform ships a publicly known, hardcoded default JWT verification key in backend/.env.default and autogpt_platform/.env.default. Because HS256 is symmetric, anyone who knows the secret can forge valid JWTs for any user or for the admin role, bypassing authentication and authorization without user interaction. This issue is fixed in version 0.8.0.

AutoGPT is a workflow automation platform for creating, deploying, and managing continuous artificial intelligence agents. From versions 0.6.23 and above, before 0.8.0, AutoGPT Platform ships a hardcoded default Fernet encryption key in backend/.env.default, which encrypts every user's OAuth tokens, API keys, and integration credentials in the User.integrations column. Anyone with read access to the database of a deployment using the default key can decrypt the stored credentials. This issue is fixed in version 0.8.0.

AutoGPT is a workflow automation platform for creating, deploying, and managing continuous artificial intelligence agents. Prior to 0.9.0, nested tools invoked by OrchestratorBlock bypass the main execution queue and are charged only after succeeding, but post-run billing still refunds a failed tool's catalogue price as a presumed pre-flight charge. Any authenticated customer can trigger failed nested calls to add uncharged credits to their balance and fund later executions using the operator's credentials. This issue is fixed in version 0.9.0.

A pooled-buffer lifetime error in Elasticsearch ES|QL Arrow response formatting can disclose data from other users' concurrent requests. An authenticated user with read access to an index who requests Arrow output containing an affected column type can receive data from indices they are not authorized to access. A temporary block can be released to a shared memory pool before deferred response writers finish using it, allowing concurrent requests to reuse the same memory. The attacker cannot select which concurrent data is disclosed.

OpenEMR is a free and open source electronic health records and medical practice management application. Prior to 8.5.0, the staff-facing portal endpoints GET api/onsiteactivityviews and GET api/onsiteactivityview/{id}, mapped to OnsiteActivityView.Query and OnsiteActivityView.Read with p_acl = p_none in portal/patient/_app_config.php, are handled without an authorization check for an authenticated staff session whose bootstrap_pid is empty. portal/patient/_machine_config.php admits that authenticated staff session, and portal/patient/fwk/libs/verysimple/Phreeze/GenericRouter.php applies the route ACL only when bootstrap_pid is nonempty, so the staff request bypasses the p_none check. OnsiteActivityViewController::Query() returns records without patient scoping, and OnsiteActivityViewController::Read() loads a record by identifier without checking ACL or ownership; OnsiteActivityViewReporter::GetCustomQuery() joins portal activity to patient demographics and includes names, dates of birth, addresses, and Social Security numbers. Any authenticated staff account, including one without the patients/demo permission, can therefore read sensitive demographics for patients represented by an existing onsite_portal_activity row; at least one such row must exist for the endpoint to return patient data. This issue is fixed in version 8.5.0.

TastyIgniter is an open-source online ordering, table reservation, and restaurant management system. Prior to 4.3.1, the Mollie payment notification handler in src/Payments/Mollie.php, processNotifyUrl(), uses a payment ID supplied with the notification to retrieve a paid transaction but does not verify that the transaction's order reference matches the order identified by the notification URL or that the transaction amount matches the order total. An ordinary customer can use a paid Mollie transaction from one order to cause a different, higher-value order to be marked paid without paying its full price. The endpoint is intentionally unauthenticated so Mollie's servers can reach it, and the request's order hash alone does not bind the fetched payment to that order. This issue is fixed in version 4.3.1.

TastyIgniter is an open-source online ordering, table reservation, and restaurant management system. Prior to 4.2.0, the User extension’s onRequestResetPassword() handler in src/Http/Controllers/Login.php calls resetPassword() and mailSendResetPasswordRequest() only when an account matches. The resulting database write and reset-email send take longer than the nonexistent-account path despite the endpoint returning the same response, allowing timing measurements against a production deployment using a synchronous queue and real SMTP transport to disclose valid staff or customer email addresses. The advisory’s local log-mailer test showed no measurable timing difference, so the signal depends on mail configuration and is useful for follow-on phishing or credential stuffing rather than direct account access. This issue is fixed in version 4.2.0.

TastyIgniter is an open-source online ordering, table reservation, and restaurant management system. Prior to 4.2.0, checkResetPasswordCode() in src/Auth/Models/User.php compares a submitted reset code with the stored 42-character token using a normal string comparison, which can return after the first differing byte instead of taking constant time. The password-reset flow exposes this comparison to remote requests, but the endpoint is rate-limited to six requests per minute per IP, and the advisory reports no live exploit or practical token-recovery demonstration. Recovering a high-entropy reset code through the constrained timing signal could permit an unauthorized password reset. This issue is fixed in version 4.2.0.

TastyIgniter is an open-source online ordering, table reservation, and restaurant management system. Prior to 4.4.4, addFromUrl() in src/Flame/Database/Attach/Media.php performs an outbound HTTP request to a caller-supplied URL and stores the response without validating the URL scheme or destination, which could enable server-side request forgery if a reachable feature passes attacker-controlled URLs to the method. The maintainer reports that no shipped first-party feature calls this method and that it is currently unreachable through product functionality, so no current attack path or impact was identified. AutoGPT is a workflow automation platform for creating, deploying, and managing continuous artificial intelligence agents. In versions 0.7.1 through 0.8.4, AutoPilot prices block calls using model-supplied input but executes them with the server-resolved credential. Supplying a syntactically valid placeholder credential causes the price rule to evaluate to zero, skipping both the balance check and debit while still running paid blocks on the operator's credential. This issue is fixed in version 0.9.0.

AutoGPT is a workflow automation platform for creating, deploying, and managing continuous artificial intelligence agents. In versions 0.7.1 through 0.8.4, chat and prompt text passed to the Claude Code CLI is pre-processed before reaching the model, bypassing AutoPilot's tool allow-list and PreToolUse hooks. In both AutoPilot's Claude Agent SDK path and the graph orchestrator block's extended_thinking SDK mode, messages starting with / execute CLI commands or bundled skills, while @<path> mentions read files or list directories on the host and attach the results to the model request. Signed-in users, members of linked chat channels, graph authors, or indirect tool output carried into turn history can make the CLI read files accessible to the copilot executor process, whose contents reach the model provider and can be repeated in replies, and run commands that compact or clear the session, switch the model, or modify the CLI's settings.json file. This issue is fixed in version 0.9.0.

A vulnerability was determined in itsourcecode Airline Reservation System 1.0. This affects an unknown part of the file admin/navbar.php. SparkyFitness before 1.12.0 contains a missing ownership check in getNutritionixHeaders that allows authenticated users to use another user's Nutritionix API credentials via the providerId parameter. Attackers who know a victim's provider UUID can call the Nutritionix search, nutrients, item, or exercise endpoints to consume the victim's paid API quota.

SparkyFitness before 1.12.0 contains a weak password change vulnerability that allows attackers with a victim's session to change the account password without supplying the current password. Attackers can send a POST request with only newPassword to /api/identity/update-password to lock out the legitimate owner and retain persistent access.

Trilium through 0.107.0 contains an sql injection vulnerability in updateNormalEntity() that allows malicious sync partners to inject SQL by supplying crafted entity names and column keys. Attackers can abuse /api/sync/changed or PUT /api/sync/update data to copy sessions, etapi_tokens and user_data into synced rows and write arbitrary database rows.

Arcane before 3.0.0 fails to enforce the requiresPasswordChange account flag on the server, allowing attackers with initial or temporary credentials to obtain fully privileged access tokens. Attackers can log in via /api/auth/login and call privileged endpoints such as POST /api/users to create users without completing the mandated password change.

Idno through 1.6.4 contains an unauthenticated blind server-side request forgery vulnerability in the /webmention/ endpoint that fetches attacker-supplied source URLs without scheme, host, or IP validation. Attackers can set target to a local page and source to loopback, private-network, or cloud metadata addresses, then infer internal service reachability from response status and timing.

Community Store for Concrete CMS before 2.8.0 contains a stored cross-site scripting vulnerability that allows unauthenticated attackers to inject script via the order email in single_pages/dashboard/store/orders.php. Attackers can place guest orders with quoted email local parts containing markup to execute script in a store manager's session when viewing the order.

CivetWeb through 1.16 built with USE_HTTP2 and enable_http2 contains a heap out-of-bounds read vulnerability in hpack_decode() in src/http2.inl. Unauthenticated remote attackers can send a crafted HEADERS frame ending with a Huffman-coded string over TLS-negotiated HTTP/2 to read one byte past the heap frame buffer.

Open5GS WebUI through 2.8.0 contains an incorrect authorization vulnerability in webui/server/routes/db.js that allows authenticated user-role accounts to modify the Account model. Attackers can send PATCH /api/db/Account/<username> setting roles to admin, overwrite password hashes, delete accounts, and read hashes to gain full administrative control.

rConfig Core 8.0.0 before 8.2.17 and rConfig Pro before 8.4.0 contain a PHP object injection vulnerability in app/Casts/EncryptStringCast.php that unserializes decrypted attributes without class restrictions. Authenticated attackers can store a serialized gadget chain in encrypted fields like device passwords, triggering command execution as the web server user when read via GET /api/devices.

rConfig Core 8.0.0 before 8.2.17 and rConfig Pro before 8.4.0 contain a stored cross-site scripting vulnerability in the Config Search View Matches dialog, which renders configuration context via v-html without escaping. Attackers can place markup in device banners, interface descriptions, ACL remarks or SNMP locations to execute script in a user's session and read stored configurations containing secrets.

rConfig Core 8.1.0 before 8.2.20 and rConfig Pro before 8.4.0 contain a missing authorization vulnerability in ExportController.php that allows authenticated users to export restricted tables. Attackers can supply excluded table names to export($table), bypassing the EXCLUDED_TABLES deny list, and obtain decrypted passwords, device credentials, and API tokens.

rConfig Core 8.0.0 before 8.2.13 and rConfig Pro before 8.4.0 contain an authorization bypass vulnerability in the users API that allows authenticated users to modify other accounts. Attackers can send a UserController::update request with an administrator's user id and new password, then log in as that administrator to take full control.

rConfig Core 8.2.19 before 8.2.22 contains a server-side request forgery vulnerability that allows authenticated users to bypass the DeviceIpIsValid loopback guard by supplying unresolved hostnames. Attackers can create a device with a hostname resolving to loopback and device_port_override 6379, causing configuration downloads to send Redis inline commands for remote code execution.

CleverReach WP before 1.5.28 contains a missing authorization vulnerability in the Article_Search controller that allows unauthenticated attackers to read non-public posts by supplying post IDs. Attackers can enumerate the id parameter in search requests to retrieve raw content of draft, pending, private, and password-protected posts and pages.

AutoGPT is a workflow automation platform for creating, deploying, and managing continuous artificial intelligence agents. In versions 0.7.1 through 0.8.4, an incomplete IPv6 blocklist in AutoGPT's outbound SSRF protection allows authenticated users to reach local or private network services. Specifically, _is_ip_blocked and BLOCKED_IP_NETWORKS in autogpt_platform/backend/backend/util/request.py fail to reject the IPv6 unspecified address :: (which connects to ::1 on Linux) as well as 6to4, NAT64, Teredo, and deprecated IPv4-compatible IPv6 encodings. An attacker can pass :: directly to blocks/sql_query_block.py or blocks/email_block.py, or point URL-fetching blocks, web fetch, MCP servers, webhooks, or OAuth at a hostname whose AAAA record resolves to ::. On backends run directly on a host, this exposes unauthenticated internal RPC services and databases listening on ::1, though the default Docker Compose and single-container deployments bind internal services to IPv4 only. This issue is fixed in version 0.9.0.

Gogs through 0.14.4 contains an information disclosure vulnerability that allows authenticated users to view private forks by querying fork listings without per-fork read checks. Attackers with read access to a private base repository can call GET /api/v1/repos/{owner}/{repo}/forks or the Forks web handler to obtain other users' private fork owners, names, descriptions and clone URLs.

Out-of-bounds write vulnerability in certain ASUS routers allows an unauthenticated nearby user to corrupt process memory, potentially resulting in a denial-of-service, via crafted LLTD packets.Refer to the ' Security Update for ASUS Router Firmware ' section on the ASUS Security Advisory for more information.

Deserialization of Untrusted Data vulnerability in ash-project ash allows an unauthenticated attacker to execute arbitrary code or inject SQL through a forged keyset pagination cursor.

Ash.Page.Keyset.filter/4 in lib/ash/page/keyset.ex decodes the client-supplied page[:after] or page[:before] cursor from Erlang external term format and rejects decoded expressions with Ash.Expr.expr?/1. That check does not examine the fields of a struct. The cast of each value against the type of its sort field accepts structs for the :ci_string, :map, :struct and :term types. A struct in the cursor value for such a sort field therefore reaches the data layer. With AshPostgres, the read passes such a struct to inspect/1, which runs the Inspect implementation of the struct module that the attacker selected. A chain of struct modules from ecto and db_connection then calls a function that the cursor names, which permits OS command execution. An %Ash.Query.Function.Fragment{} inside an %Ash.CiString{} value is written into the SQL query as raw text.

This issue affects ash: from 3.31.3 before 3.38.0.

XML::Sig versions before 0.74 for Perl allow code execution via a document's Algorithm attribute that verify resolves to a function name and calls.

The text after the last `#` in the DigestMethod and SignatureMethod Algorithm attributes is looked up with Digest::SHA->can. That returns a code reference for any fully qualified function name, Perl builtins in the CORE namespace included. The digest function is called on the canonical form of the referenced element, so the document picks both the function and its argument.

An attacker who can submit a signed document can run a command as the verifying process.

FFmpeg before 9.1 contains an uninitialized memory use vulnerability in asfrtp_parse_packet() in libavformat/rtpdec_asf.c that allows malicious RTP sources to leak heap contents by supplying an oversized ASF packet length. Attackers controlling an RTSP server with an x-asf-pf payload can set len_off beyond the RTP payload so the ASF demuxer returns stale heap memory as demuxed media data.

FFmpeg before 9.1 contains an information disclosure vulnerability in the MXG demuxer's mxg_read_packet() that allows attackers to leak uninitialized heap memory through truncated marker segments. Attackers can supply a crafted MXG file ending in a truncated APP13 segment with a large declared length, causing uninitialized heap contents to be emitted as audio packet payload, for example into remuxed output files.

FFmpeg before 9.1 contains a stack out-of-bounds read vulnerability in ff_h264_parse_framesize() in libavformat/rtpdec_h264.c when parsing an SDP a=framesize attribute lacking a height. Attackers controlling an RTSP server DESCRIBE response or a crafted .sdp file can make atoi() read past the line buffer, crashing clients or parsing stale stack bytes.

FFmpeg before 9.1 contains a heap buffer overflow vulnerability in modplug_read_header() in libavformat/libmodplug.c that allocates the buffer using max_size instead of sz. When max_size is set to 0, attackers can supply crafted module files that avio_read() copies into a zero-sized buffer, causing memory corruption, crashes, or possible code execution.

FFmpeg before 9.1 contains an uninitialized memory vulnerability in nist_read_header() in libavformat/nistspheredec.c, where an inverted ff_alloc_extradata() return check leaves the embedded-shorten extradata byte uninitialized. Attackers can supply a crafted NIST SPHERE file declaring pcm,embedded-shorten coding to leak an uninitialized heap byte into copied output or trigger a NULL pointer write on allocation failure.

FFmpeg 8.0 before 9.1 contains an improper URL scheme validation vulnerability in the WHIP muxer that allows malicious WHIP servers to create or truncate local files via the Location header. Attackers can return a file: URL that dispose_session() opens read-write with truncation on teardown, destroying arbitrary user-writable files or redirecting requests to other protocols.

FFmpeg before 9.1 contains an out-of-bounds write vulnerability in ogg_buffer_data() in libavformat/oggenc.c because ogg_buffer_page() leaves a full page current after failed allocation. When page allocation fails, a memset with length (size_t)-1 or an overflowing memcpy writes past the segment table, causing heap memory corruption and crashes when writing Ogg output.

FFmpeg before 9.1 contains an uninitialized memory disclosure vulnerability in vmd_read_packet() in libavformat/sierravmd.c that leaves 16 packet bytes unwritten for Indeo3 frames. Attackers can supply a crafted VMD file with Indeo3 video to expose leftover heap contents in demuxed packets, such as stream-copied output files.

FFmpeg before 9.1 contains an XML injection vulnerability in ttml_write_header() in libavformat/ttmlenc.c that writes stream language metadata unescaped into the xml:lang attribute. Attackers can supply media files, such as Matroska subtitle tracks with crafted Language values, to inject markup into converted TTML documents and alter downstream parsing or rendering.

FFmpeg before 9.1 contains an integer overflow vulnerability in the split_planes size check of write_packet() in libavformat/img2enc.c that allows out-of-bounds heap reads. Attackers can supply a crafted input whose rawvideo stream declares very large width and height, remuxed into .y image files, to leak heap memory into output files or crash the application.

FFmpeg before 9.1 contains a NULL pointer dereference vulnerability in libavformat/mmst.c that allows malicious MMS servers to crash clients by sending malformed ASF headers. Attackers can send an ASF header lacking a packet size or stream properties, causing mms_open() to return success after freeing state and crash on first read.

FFmpeg before 9.1 contains an information disclosure vulnerability in amf_get_field_value2() in libavformat/rtmppkt.c that NUL-terminates truncated AMF strings at the declared length instead of bytes read. A malicious RTMP server, or connecting client in listen mode, can send truncated onStatus or _error strings to leak uninitialized stack memory through log messages.

FFmpeg before 9.1 contains a NULL pointer dereference vulnerability in the AVIF muxer in libavformat/movenc.c that allows attackers to crash the application through streams with unknown pixel formats. Attackers can supply a crafted input whose video stream is stream-copied to AVIF, causing unchecked av_pix_fmt_desc_get() results to be dereferenced, resulting in denial of service.

FFmpeg before 9.1 contains an out-of-bounds write vulnerability in build_frame_code() in libavformat/nutenc.c that allows attackers to corrupt the header_len[] array by supplying inputs with many audio streams. Attackers can remux a crafted input with many audio streams to NUT, causing out-of-bounds reads past static header tables and crashing the application.

FFmpeg 8.0 before 9.1 contains a use of uninitialized memory vulnerability in opus_parse_packet() in libavformat/rtpdec_opus.c that reads the Opus TOC byte from stale buffer memory when parsing empty RTP payloads. A malicious RTSP server or RTP sender can deliver an empty Opus payload to cause incorrect packet durations and leak bits of stale memory through pkt->duration.

FFmpeg 7.0 before 9.1 contains an out-of-bounds read vulnerability in dvdvideo_audio_stream_add_all() in libavformat/dvdvideodec.c when parsing menu audio streams. Attackers can supply a crafted DVD image whose menu IFO declares more than 8 audio streams, reading past the audio_control array and crashing applications.

FFmpeg before 9.1 contains an uninitialized memory disclosure vulnerability in dxa_read_packet() in libavformat/dxa.c that ignores short avio_read() results for CMAP palette data. Attackers can supply a crafted DXA stream over a stalling network source so uninitialized stack bytes are copied into returned video packets and decoded frames.

FFmpeg 9.0 before 9.1 contains a NULL pointer dereference vulnerability in dash_read_header() in libavformat/dashdec.c when building LCEVC stream groups without checking for a missing codecs string. Attackers can supply a crafted MPD manifest with a representation declaring a dependencyId but no codecs attribute to crash applications using the DASH demuxer.

FFmpeg before 9.1 contains an infinite loop vulnerability in ff_rtp_send_vc2hq() in libavformat/rtpenc_vc2hq.c that accepts a Dirac next parse offset of zero. Attackers can supply crafted Dirac/VC-2 video remuxed to the RTP muxer, causing the parsing pointer to never advance and consume CPU indefinitely.

FFmpeg before 9.1 contains a heap-based buffer overflow vulnerability in peak_init_writer() and wav_write_packet() in libavformat/wavenc.c that allows attackers to corrupt heap memory by supplying audio with zero channels. Attackers can provide a crafted PCM stream declaring no channels for WAV output with peak envelope enabled, causing out-of-bounds writes past peak_maxpos and peak_maxneg arrays, crashes, and potential code execution.

FFmpeg before 9.1 contains a double free vulnerability in the fill_marker() function of libavformat/imf_cpl.c that frees a Marker label without clearing the pointer when default scope allocation fails. Attackers can supply a crafted Composition Playlist with a Marker Label lacking a scope attribute, triggering a second free in imf_marker_free() under memory pressure and causing memory corruption or a crash.

FFmpeg before 9.1 contains a NULL pointer dereference vulnerability in avformat_stream_group_create() in libavformat/options.c that sets the group type before allocating parameters. Attackers can supply crafted HEIF/AVIF files whose tile grid parsing under allocation failure makes ff_free_stream_group() dereference a NULL tile_grid, crashing the application.

FFmpeg before 9.1 contains a stack-based buffer overflow vulnerability in ff_rtmp_packet_write() in libavformat/rtmppkt.c that allows malicious RTMP servers to overflow a 16-byte header buffer. Attackers can send a Set Chunk Size packet on a high channel id with an extended timestamp, which handle_chunk_size() echoes back, corrupting the publishing client's stack.

FFmpeg before 9.1 contains a NULL pointer dereference vulnerability in rdt_parse_packet() in libavformat/rdt.c that allows remote attackers to crash applications by omitting the ASMRuleBook SDP attribute. Attackers can serve an RTSP session selecting RDT transport without ASMRuleBook, then send an RDT data packet to crash ffmpeg or ffprobe.

FFmpeg before 9.1 contains an uninitialized memory disclosure vulnerability in rfc4175_handle_packet() in libavformat/rtpdec_rfc4175.c that leaks heap contents into decoded video frames. Attackers can send RTP streams containing only some scan lines of a frame, leaving av_malloc buffer bytes uninitialized and exposing process heap memory in displayed, stored or re-streamed video.

FFmpeg before 9.1 contains a signed integer overflow vulnerability in libavformat/dashdec.c that allows attackers to crash applications by supplying a crafted DASH manifest. Attackers can craft an MPD manifest with very long BaseURL and SegmentTemplate strings to overflow max_url_size, causing undersized URL allocations and denial of service.

FFmpeg before 9.1 contains an XML injection vulnerability in write_adaptation_set() in libavformat/webmdashenc.c that writes stream language metadata unescaped into the AdaptationSet lang attribute. Attackers can supply crafted WebM files whose track language contains quotes or angle brackets to inject attributes or elements, controlling segment URLs and representations in generated MPD manifests.

FFmpeg before 9.1 contains an uninitialized memory vulnerability in vpk_read_header() in libavformat/vpk.c that computes a last block size not divisible by the channel count. Attackers can supply a crafted VPK file with a large channel count so the last audio packet exposes leftover heap memory contents.

FFmpeg before 9.1 contains an integer overflow in send_picture() of libavformat/rtpenc_vc2hq.c that leaves the bit reader without a buffer, causing a NULL pointer dereference. Attackers can supply a Dirac/VC-2 stream with a picture data unit of about 256 MiB or more to crash applications packetizing it to RTP.

FFmpeg before 9.1 contains an out-of-bounds read vulnerability in mxf_write_d10_audio_packet() in libavformat/mxfenc.c because mxf_init() accepts unsupported D-10 audio codecs. Attackers can supply a crafted input with a non-PCM multichannel audio stream remuxed to D-10 MXF to leak heap memory into the output file or crash the application.

FFmpeg through 9.1 contains an insecure default configuration in the zmq and azmq filters of libavfilter/f_zmq.c that binds an unauthenticated command socket to all interfaces on TCP port 5555. Remote attackers can send 'TARGET COMMAND [ARG]' messages passed to avfilter_graph_send_command() to change filter runtime parameters and alter processed audio or video.

FFmpeg before 9.1 contains a heap out-of-bounds write vulnerability in the deflicker filter that lets attackers corrupt heap memory via unclamped high bit depth luma samples. Attackers can supply crafted video whose luma values exceed the nominal depth, making calc_avgy16() increment counters past the histogram allocation, causing crashes or possibly code execution.

FFmpeg before 9.1 contains a heap out-of-bounds read vulnerability in filter_slice_rgba_planar() that allows attackers to read beyond lookup tables using unmasked high bit depth planar samples. Attackers can supply crafted video with samples exceeding the nominal depth, passed unchanged by rawvideo, to crash the application or leak heap contents into output video.

FFmpeg 4.4 before 9.1 contains a heap out-of-bounds read and write vulnerability in libavfilter/vf_deband.c that allows attackers to corrupt heap memory by sending a runtime coupling command. Attackers can send a 'deband coupling 1' command via sendcmd or an unauthenticated zmq filter, making chroma planes be processed at luma dimensions to crash the process or potentially execute code.

FFmpeg before 9.1 contains a heap out-of-bounds write and read vulnerability in the tmidequalizer filter that allows attackers to corrupt memory by supplying high bit depth samples exceeding the nominal maximum. Attackers can craft planar 9, 10, 12 or 14 bit video so compute_histogram16() and apply_contrast_change16() index unclamped samples, crashing applications, corrupting the heap, and leaking heap contents.

FFmpeg before 9.1 contains a heap out-of-bounds write vulnerability in libavfilter/vf_signalstats.c that allows attackers to corrupt heap memory by supplying high bit depth samples exceeding the nominal maximum. Attackers can craft planar 9 to 14 bit YUV video whose unclamped samples or saturation values index past histogram ends, crashing applications or possibly executing code.

FFmpeg 7.1 before 9.1 contains an out-of-bounds read vulnerability in libavfilter/vf_scale.c that allows attackers to read past the filter input array by sending width or height commands using ref variables. Attackers can send such commands via sendcmd scripts or unauthenticated zmq or azmq filters, causing config_props() to dereference an invalid pointer and crash the process.

FFmpeg before 9.1 contains a heap out-of-bounds write vulnerability in libavfilter/vf_readeia608.c because build_histogram() does not clamp high bit depth luma samples to the nominal maximum. Attackers can supply crafted 9, 10, 12 or 14 bit gray or YUV video to corrupt heap memory, causing crashes or possibly code execution.

FFmpeg before 9.1 contains a heap out-of-bounds read vulnerability in libavfilter/vf_lut2.c because the second input's pixel format is unrestricted when the output depth option is set. Attackers can supply crafted media such as monoblack BMP or PBM images to index beyond lookup tables, crashing applications or leaking heap contents into output video.

FFmpeg before 9.1 contains a heap buffer overflow vulnerability in recv_msg() of the zmq and azmq filters that allows unauthenticated network attackers to corrupt memory by sending oversized command messages. Attackers can send a 4 GiB message to the default listening port, truncating the int buffer size so memcpy() writes past the heap allocation and crashes FFmpeg.

FFmpeg 4.3 before 9.1 contains a heap out-of-bounds read and write vulnerability in the dynaudnorm filter because cqueue_resize() miscalculates gain history queue element counts when gausssize changes at runtime. FFmpeg before 9.1 contains an out-of-bounds read vulnerability in the lut1d filter in libavfilter/vf_lut3d.c that allows attackers to read heap memory by supplying planar high bit depth samples above the nominal depth.
